strategy.intent: Define a family of interchangeable algorithms behind one common interface and let a context select and delegate to one at runtime, so the algorithm varies independently of the client that uses it.

invariants.rationale: Interchangeability is the whole point. The context can hold ANY member of the family only because every concrete_strategy conforms to the same interface. A concrete_strategy that does not implement th

THE load-bearing constraint. The context must couple only to the strategy abstraction so algorithms vary independently of the client. Any direct context->concrete_strategy edge (naming a concrete clas

This is the defining behavioral fact: the context runs the variable algorithm by delegating to the held strategy rather than implementing it inline. Without a delegation edge there is no Strategy — ju

The context must hold the strategy by the abstract interface type. That field IS the substitution seam where a concrete_strategy is plugged in at runtime; if the context holds no strategy reference (o

Selection authority belongs to the client. If the context instantiates a specific concrete_strategy, it re-hardcodes the algorithm choice and can no longer be reconfigured from outside, degenerating b

strategy.conformant_example: Checkout shipping cost. strategy = interface ShippingCost { cost(order): Money }. concrete_strategy = FlatRateShipping, WeightBasedShipping, FreeShipping — each `implements ShippingCost`. context = Checkout, which holds a field `ShippingCost shipping` (composes strategy) and computes totals via `shipping.cost(order)` (delegates_to strategy); Checkout's source never names any concrete shipping class (depends_on strategy only). client = OrderService, which does `new WeightBasedShipping()` (creates concrete_strategy) and passes it into `new Checkout(weightBased)` (references context). Adding a NextDayShipping algorithm means writing one new class that implements ShippingCost and having OrderService inject it — Checkout is untouched. Every invariant holds.

drift_example.what_drifts: To 'simplify', Checkout gains a method `computeShipping(String method, Order o)` whose body is `if (method.equals("flat")) return new FlatRateShipping().cost(o); else if (method.equals("weight")) return new WeightBasedShipping().cost(o); ...`. The ShippingCost field is dropped; Checkout now names and instantiates the concrete algorithms directly.
drift_example.breaks_invariant: Violates the load-bearing invariant FORBIDDEN: context depends_on concrete_strategy (relation_type=depends_on, from_role=context, to_role=concrete_strategy) — Checkout now has direct edges to FlatRateShipping and WeightBasedShipping. It simultaneously trips FORBIDDEN: context creates concrete_strategy and drops REQUIRED: context composes strategy / delegates_to strategy. Concretely, adding NextDayShipping now requires editing Checkout's switch, which is exactly the coupling the pattern exists to prevent — the geometry has drifted out of Strategy into a conditional monolith.

layered.archi_kind: architectural style — layered / n-tier (closed layers, with dependency inversion at the infrastructure seam)
layered.intent: Partition a system into ordered layers whose source dependencies flow strictly inward/downward — presentation on top, then application, then the pure domain core, with infrastructure inverted onto domain-owned ports — so business logic never depends on UI or technical detail and each layer stays independently testable and replaceable.

invariants.rationale: Establishes the single legal entry path into the system; if presentation does not enter through application there is no layering to enforce and the top layer will reach deeper layers directly.
The application layer exists to orchestrate the domain; this edge is the spine of the layering. Its absence means business logic has leaked upward into presentation or downward into infrastructure.

Dependency inversion: concrete technical adapters must implement domain-owned abstractions. This is exactly what makes the domain-purity forbidden below satisfiable — the core declares a need and infr

KEYSTONE. If the core imports the DB/ORM/HTTP client, business logic becomes coupled to technical detail, cannot be unit-tested without I/O, and infrastructure can no longer be swapped — the layered p
No upward dependency: the core must not know the use cases that orchestrate it, or it becomes un-reusable across workflows and forms an import cycle.
No upward dependency: the core must not know the UI/transport, or business rules become bound to a delivery mechanism.
No upward dependency: an application service that references a controller or view inverts control and couples the use case to its caller's transport.
Closed-layer rule: presentation must not skip the application layer to manipulate domain entities directly, or use-case orchestration and its invariants get duplicated in controllers.
Presentation must never touch the persistence/technical layer directly (e.g. a controller running raw SQL or opening a DB session), bypassing all business rules and validation.
No upward dependency: infrastructure is a leaf that only implements ports; if an adapter calls an application service it re-enters the system from the bottom and creates a cycle spanning every layer.

layered.conformant_example: A web checkout. `OrderController` (presentation) depends_on `PlaceOrderService` (application). `PlaceOrderService` depends_on the `Order` aggregate (domain) and the `OrderRepository` interface (domain_port). The `Order` entity enforces its own invariants and imports nothing from any other layer; the domain layer declares `OrderRepository`. `PostgresOrderRepository` (infrastructure) implements `OrderRepository`. Every source edge points inward/downward — presentation→application→domain, plus infrastructure→domain_port — so the domain has zero outward imports and `Order` can be unit-tested against an in-memory fake repository. The gate finds all required edges present and no forbidden edge: STAYS IN PATTERN.

drift_example.what_drifts: To 'simplify persistence', the `Order` domain entity gains a `save()` method that imports the ORM session / `PostgresOrderRepository` from the infrastructure layer and writes itself (an Active-Record shortcut). A new source edge domain→infrastructure now exists in the filled geometry.
drift_example.breaks_invariant: FORBIDDEN depends_on from domain to infrastructure (the dependency-inversion / domain-purity keystone invariant). The core now imports the DB layer, so it can no longer be tested or run without Postgres and infrastructure is no longer swappable; the Prolog gate emits residue naming exactly this edge — forbidden(depends_on, domain, infrastructure) — DRIFTED OUT.

hexagonal.intent: Isolate the domain/application core from delivery mechanisms and infrastructure by having the core depend only on interfaces (ports) it owns, while every concrete technology lives in an adapter that plugs into a port — so all dependencies point inward and infrastructure can be swapped, mocked, or replaced without touching the core.

invariants.rationale: The port must be DEFINED inside the core, not in the infrastructure layer. If the outbound interface lives in the persistence/adapter package, the dependency arrow silently inverts (core → infra packa

Dependency inversion: the core states its infrastructure needs abstractly, as a port it owns. This edge is the mechanism that lets any driven_adapter (real DB, in-memory fake, mock) be substituted wit
Every outbound adapter must realize a port. An infrastructure class that does NOT implement a port is technology wired straight into the core, which defeats substitutability and testing in isolation.
The use-case logic must sit behind the primary port so actors reach it only through the port; this is what lets HTTP, CLI, and test harnesses all drive the identical core logic.
Inbound adapters must call the core only through the primary port interface, keeping the delivery mechanism decoupled from and replaceable independently of the concrete use-case implementation.

THE load-bearing constraint. A core → concrete-adapter edge points OUTWARD, dragging infrastructure into the domain and destroying testability and substitutability. All dependencies must point inward;

Same inward-only rule at the far end: importing a SQL/HTTP/SMTP client or vendor SDK directly in domain code couples business rules to a specific technology and makes the core impossible to run withou

The core must not know its callers. The inbound direction is actor → adapter → port → core; if the core references the controller/CLI it is coupled to one delivery mechanism and can no longer be drive

hexagonal.conformant_example: An order service. domain_core = OrderService; driving_port = PlaceOrderUseCase (interface, in the core package); driven_port = OrderRepository and PaymentGateway (interfaces, in the core package); driving_adapter = OrderRestController; driven_adapter = PostgresOrderRepository (implements OrderRepository) and StripePaymentAdapter (implements PaymentGateway); external_system = Postgres and the Stripe API; primary_actor = the HTTP client. Wiring: OrderRestController depends on and delegates to PlaceOrderUseCase; OrderService implements PlaceOrderUseCase and, for all side-effects, depends only on the OrderRepository and PaymentGateway ports; PostgresOrderRepository implements OrderRepository and is the sole place the JDBC/pg driver is imported. The domain_core package's import list contains no adapter, no framework, and no vendor SDK — every arrow points inward, so the core compiles and unit-tests with in-memory fakes and Postgres/Stripe can be swapped without touching it.

drift_example.what_drifts: OrderService needs to filter orders with a Postgres-specific full-text query, so a developer imports PostgresOrderRepository directly and calls its pgFullTextSearch() method instead of adding a method to the OrderRepository port. The concrete adapter class (and transitively the pg driver) now appears in the domain_core package's import list.
drift_example.breaks_invariant: FORBIDDEN | depends_on | domain_core → driven_adapter. The core now has an outward-pointing edge to a concrete outbound adapter, violating the inward-only dependency rule: OrderService can no longer be compiled or unit-tested without Postgres present, and the adapter is no longer substitutable — the gate emits this exact edge as residue.

observer.intent: Let a subject notify an open, dynamically-changing set of dependents of its state changes without the subject knowing their concrete types, so publishers and subscribers evolve independently.

invariants.rationale: The fan-out — one state change, N abstract update() calls — must exist and go through the abstract role. It is the pattern's whole purpose; without a subject→observer notify edge there is no publish-s

The load-bearing decoupling. If notify() calls a concrete observer's method by its concrete type, the subject must be edited/recompiled for every new subscriber kind — the fan-out stops being open/clo

The subject must be blind to concrete subscriber types — no field, import, cast, or instanceof. Any concrete reference re-couples publisher to subscriber and defeats independent evolution, even if not
The subject must hold its subscribers in a collection typed to the abstract observer so it can add/remove/iterate them without knowing concrete types; this is where the dynamic subscriber set lives.

The subscriber collection must be typed abstractly. A List<ConcreteObserver> bakes one subscriber type into the subject and makes heterogeneous subscribers impossible — a structural leak distinct from
notify() invokes update() polymorphically over abstract observers; a concrete_observer that does not implement observer cannot sit in the collection and forces the subject to know it by concrete type
State-changing publishers must inherit the abstract attach/detach/notify machinery so all notification flows through the one abstract loop rather than ad-hoc per-publisher wiring.

observer.conformant_example: WeatherData (concrete_subject) extends Subject and holds List<Observer> observers (composes subject→observer). Its notifyObservers() loops that list calling o.update() (notifies subject→observer). CurrentConditionsDisplay and StatisticsDisplay each implement Observer (implements concrete_observer→observer), register via weatherData.registerObserver(this) (depends_on concrete_observer→subject), and hold a WeatherData handle to pull temperature/humidity after update() (references concrete_observer→concrete_subject). WeatherData contains no field, import, or method call naming any concrete display — adding a ForecastDisplay requires zero edits to WeatherData. STAYS IN PATTERN.

drift_example.what_drifts: WeatherData.notifyObservers() is rewritten to call this.phoneDisplay.updatePhone() and this.webDisplay.updateWeb() directly — naming each concrete display type and its bespoke method — instead of iterating List<Observer> and calling observer.update(). Adding any new display type now requires editing WeatherData and recompiling the subject.
drift_example.breaks_invariant: FORBIDDEN notifies subject→concrete_observer (behavioral leak) — and simultaneously FORBIDDEN references subject→concrete_observer, since WeatherData now holds phoneDisplay/webDisplay fields of concrete type. The subject names concrete observers, re-coupling publisher to subscriber.

repository.archi_kind: persistence pattern (DDD tactical / architectural boundary pattern)
repository.intent: Give the domain a collection-like abstraction for loading and saving aggregates so it depends on a repository interface expressed in domain terms, never on the ORM/SQL/persistence details that back it.

invariants.rationale: Substitutability is the payoff: because every backing implements the same domain-declared interface, a SQL repo, an in-memory test double, or a different store all stand in without the domain changing

The dependency inversion itself: the domain reaches persistence only through the abstraction it owns. If the client depends on nothing here, it is either bypassing repositories or fetching data some o

THE keystone. If the domain names the concrete (DB-backed) repository, the inversion collapses — changing or swapping persistence now forces edits inside the domain, and tests can no longer substitute

The entire reason the repository exists is that the domain never sees the ORM/session/SQL. A direct client→persistence edge means the repository is isolating nothing; persistence has leaked straight i

The interface must be declared in domain terms. The moment a method signature accepts or returns a persistence type (a Session, a Query, a Row, an ORM filter), every consumer transitively couples to t

A repository is a collection of aggregate roots: its operations must traffic in domain objects, not DTOs or persistence rows. If the interface deals in rows/tuples instead, it is a data-access object,

repository.conformant_example: A Python DDD app. `Order` is the domain_model (aggregate root). `OrderRepository` is the repository_interface — an ABC with `add(order: Order) -> None`, `get(order_id: OrderId) -> Order`, `find_unfulfilled() -> list[Order]`, all typed in domain terms. `SqlAlchemyOrderRepository` is the concrete_repository: it `implements` `OrderRepository` and holds a SQLAlchemy `Session` (persistence_mechanism), translating `get` into `session.get(Order, ...)`. `PlaceOrderService` is the domain_client: its constructor takes an `OrderRepository`, it imports only `OrderRepository` and `Order` (never `sqlalchemy` or `SqlAlchemyOrderRepository`), and calls `repo.get(...)` / `repo.add(...)`. Swapping in `InMemoryOrderRepository` for a unit test requires zero change to `PlaceOrderService`. Every invariant holds: concrete implements interface, client depends on interface, interface references only Order, and no domain-side edge touches the Session.

drift_example.what_drifts: PlaceOrderService needs a query the interface does not expose (say, orders by customer within a date window). Instead of adding a domain-worded method to OrderRepository, the service imports SqlAlchemyOrderRepository, pulls its `.session`, and runs `session.query(Order).filter(Order.customer_id == cid, Order.created >= start)` inline. Now the application service holds a live SQLAlchemy Session and an ORM query, so persistence details sit directly inside domain logic.
drift_example.breaks_invariant: FORBIDDEN depends_on: domain_client -> persistence_mechanism (and, via the direct import, FORBIDDEN depends_on: domain_client -> concrete_repository). The gate emits residue naming domain_client->persistence_mechanism as the violated forbidden edge: the domain no longer reaches storage only through the repository interface.

pipes-filters.intent: Process a data stream as a linear (or branching) chain of independent transformation stages (filters) that communicate only through connectors (pipes), so stages can be reordered, replaced, and reused without any stage knowing about another.

invariants.rationale: THE load-bearing constraint: dataflow between stages must be pipe-mediated. A direct filter→filter dataflow edge hard-wires two stages together, so you can no longer reorder, remove, or insert a stage

Filters are black boxes independent of one another. If one filter names/references another's type or instance, it now knows its neighbor's identity and interface, destroying reuse (the filter can't be

A direct invocation is control coupling that bypasses the pipe (and its buffering/back-pressure). It turns a dataflow topology into a call graph, so the pipeline's order is no longer data-driven and r

No build-time or data dependency may exist between filters; each must be independently deployable and unit-testable against a pipe stub. A depends_on edge means a filter cannot be built or run without
Every filter's ONLY output channel must be a pipe. Requiring this (together with forbidding filter→filter) is what positively guarantees 'connected only through pipes': a filter with no outgoing pipe

Every filter must be fed by a pipe on its input side — a filter's only inbound channel is a pipe. This closes the loop: with both the input and output of every filter forced through pipes, no side cha

Every filter must honor the same uniform read-transform-write contract. Without a common interface, filters are not freely interchangeable at a pipe and the reorder/replace guarantee is only accidenta
Even the origin of data must emit into a pipe rather than wiring directly into a filter, so the source is itself swappable and the first stage is not privileged/coupled to a specific producer.

pipes-filters.conformant_example: A Unix-style log-analysis pipeline: `cat access.log | grep ' 200 ' | cut -d' ' -f7 | sort | uniq -c`. Mapping — source = the `cat` file reader emitting bytes; filters = `grep`, `cut`, `sort`, `uniq`, each an independent process; pipes = the four `|` shell pipes carrying line/byte streams; sink = the terminal/stdout writer; pipeline = the shell command that wires them; filter_interface = the stdin→transform→stdout byte-stream contract every command honors. `grep` has no idea `cut` exists downstream; each reads only its stdin and writes only its stdout; every connection is a `|`. You can reorder (`sort` before `cut`), drop `uniq`, or splice in `tr` with zero edits to any other stage — all invariants hold: no filter routes_to/calls/references/depends_on another, every filter routes_to a pipe and is fed by a pipe, and every filter implements the stdin/stdout interface.

drift_example.what_drifts: In an image-processing pipeline (decode → resize → watermark → encode), the `resize` filter is optimized to avoid a buffer copy by importing the `watermark` module and invoking `watermark.apply(frame)` directly on each frame — then only that result is written out. This introduces two illegal edges from resize to watermark: a routes_to edge (frames flow straight from resize into watermark, not through the resize→pipe→watermark pipe) and a calls/references edge (resize now names and invokes watermark).
drift_example.breaks_invariant: FORBIDDEN filter --routes_to--> filter (kind=forbidden, relation_type=routes_to, from_role=filter, to_role=filter): resize connects directly to watermark instead of through a pipe. (It also trips the sibling FORBIDDEN filter--calls-->filter and filter--references-->filter edges.) Consequence: watermark can no longer be disabled, reordered after encode, or swapped for `blur` without editing resize's source — the reconfigurable dataflow topology is gone, which is exactly the residue the Prolog gate names.
